hypothesis: The fresh-install kernel venv bootstrap is dominated by the per-skill uv invocations: sync_python_skills installs every missing Python skill with its own `uv pip install --editable` child process, and each call pays a process plus PEP 517 build-backend startup for a metadata-only editable install.
approach: Baseline first, phase-split via a PATH uv wrapper (each uv invocation logged t0/t1/rc/args) + .bootstrap-version marker mtime + pre/mid/post CPU calibration on a fresh install tree (assemble_artifacts.py, fixture catalog) at the pure tip; cold vs warm uv cache; standalone uv attribution. Candidate: batch every missing skill into ONE `uv pip install --editable ...` invocation in crates/pa-core/src/kernel/bootstrap/venv.rs sync_python_skills; on batch failure fall back to the per-skill loop (identical per-skill warnings, one broken skill never blocks the rest). Two unit tests with a fake uv (batch success skips installed skills; broken-skill fallback).

Wire/output parity: kernel receipt + KERNEL_BOOT_OK both arms; venv tree byte-size identical; uv call shape change (12 -> 4) is the intended change. Install bytes +96,816 binary / +60,012 tarball-gz (+0.046% binary) at the folded head. Linux x86_64 measured; macOS arm64 unmeasured.
